LESSON: LOCATION, POSITION AND SIZE OF KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.2: Location, Position and Size of Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Location, Position and Size of Kenya, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How would you give the location and position of Kenya?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related the location, position and size of Kenya,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Location, Position and Size of Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: acquires knowledge on their country as learners discuss the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours.

● Learning to learn: engages in self-driven tasks as learners compose songs and poems about Kenya and her neighbors.

Values:
● Patriotism: love of their country as learners compose songs and poems about Kenya and her neighbours.

● Peace: respect for diversity as learners discuss the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self-esteem: speaking positively about self, as learners discuss the importance of Kenya in relation to her neighbours.

● Social cohesion: co-exist, as learners discuss the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours.

Link to other learning areas:

● Mathematics: learners relate to skills acquired in Mathematics as they find out the size of Kenya using digital resources and share in class.

● Creative arts: learners apply drawing skills learnt in Creative Arts as they draw a map of Kenya and indicate her neighbours.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Atlas, KSL Dictionary, print and electronic maps, drawing materials, digital devices, approved textbooks,
